comments.text: A 'multi-point' checklist from ANYONE selling you a car is worthless.  I once bought a truck from a Ford dealership that had the "Ford Pre-owned certification".  I found out a day later the truck had been in a collision and had several thousands of dollars of repairs done to it.  Because my insurance company told me, when I called them to give them the VIN and get my insurance in order, that it had been smashed.  The vehicle looked good, so the repairs were obviously well done.  The problem is, loss of value.  Because eventually if I went to sell it, that accident info would likely come up, therefore making the truck worth thousands less than it would normally be.  Fortunately the dealer took it back and tore up the sales contract the next day when I went in and raised hell.   DO NOT TRUST any report from anyone selling you a car.  A CarFax report is a good idea. HOWEVER that accident on that truck I bought did NOT show up in the CarFax !  So CarFax is not always accurate either!
